title: SimulCost: A Cost-Aware Benchmark and Toolkit for Automating Physics Simulations with LLMs
claim: A benchmark combines curated tasks, a solver suite, an agent loop and cost-aware evaluation into one end-to-end evaluation system.
layout: 4 columns left-to-right, colored headers, funnel plus simulator mosaic plus feedback loop
description: A wide four-stage banner with colored headers: Dataset Curation, Solver Playground, LLM Agent, Evaluation. On the left, textbooks, online repositories and research papers feed a funnel (solver development, reference solution search, variation design, filtering). A summary box follows (12 simulators, 3 domains, 3 accuracy levels, 4816 tasks). The center is a mosaic of simulation output thumbnails: Euler 1D/2D, MPM, FEM, Navier-Stokes, Burgers, Diffusion-Reaction, Heat 1D/2D, Hasegawa-Mima, Epoch. On the right, a robot icon receives a system and user prompt. It makes tool calls with single-round and multi-round arrows and simulation feedback. A reference solution badge is compared against outputs. Evaluation shows heatmaps labeled too coarse (cheap, differs too much) and too fine (okay but expensive).
caption: \textbf{Overview of \ours{}.} Our benchmark evaluates LLM agents on cost-sensitive parameter tuning across 12 physics simulators spanning fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, and plasma physics. Given a simulation task, tuning mode, and accuracy requirement, the LLM proposes tunable parameters in either single-round (initial guess) or multi-round (trial-and-error) mode. The challenge is balancing accuracy and cost: overly coarse parameters fail accuracy requirements, while overly fine parameters waste computation.
abstract: Evaluating LLM agents for scientific tasks has focused on token costs while ignoring tool-use costs like simulation time and experimental resources. As a result, metrics like pass@k become impractical under realistic budget constraints. To address this gap, we introduce SimulCost, the first benchmark targeting cost-sensitive parameter tuning in physics simulations. SimulCost compares LLM tuning cost-sensitive parameters against traditional scanning approach in both accuracy and computational cost, spanning 2,643 single-round (initial guess) and 2,304 multi-round (adjustment by trial-and-error) tasks across 11 simulators from fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, and plasma physics, whose costs are analytically defined and platform-independent. A twelfth simulator, a production plasma code measurable only by wall clock, is reported separately. Frontier LLMs achieve 45-62% success rates in single-round mode, dropping to 34-50% under high accuracy requirements, rendering their initial guesses unreliable especially for high accuracy tasks. Multi-round mode improves rates to 66-81%, but LLMs are 1.5-2.7x slower than traditional scanning, making them uneconomical choices. We also investigate parameter group correlations for knowledge transfer potential, and the impact of in-context examples and reasoning effort, providing practical implications for deployment and fine-tuning. We open-source SimulCost as a static benchmark and extensible toolkit to facilitate research on improving cost-aware agentic designs for physics simulations, and for expanding new simulation environments. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Rose-STL-Lab/SimulCost-Bench
